excluded_questions.purpose: Questions dropped from scoring for every engine so no model is graded on a case another model was structurally unable to attempt.
excluded_questions.frozen_corpus: unchanged; selected-rows.jsonl.gz and its sha256 are untouched. Exclusion is applied at scoring time only.
excluded_questions.criterion: A row is excluded for reach only when nearly the whole field cannot attempt it. A limit that one model has and others do not is that model's result, not a defect in the suite, and is never grounds for removing the row.
excluded_questions.provenance: Defects verified against the upstream sources; cais/mmlu ships the duplicate choices verbatim and the builder applies no normalisation to MMLU.

rules.rule: Two or more options are byte-identical. A distinct-options contract (Solomon) refuses these outright, so scoring them rewards engines with looser input validation.
The correct answer is itself one of the identical strings, so a textually correct choice is scored wrong at chance. Unanswerable.
MuSR ships "pantry" and "pantry " as separate locations; the trailing space carries no task meaning.
As above, and the gold is the space-variant.

Rows longer than almost every entrant can accept. Measured across the 27 completed sweeps, 14 answer none of them and only 4 answer all; the rest manage a fifth. They cannot separate models, and the group-completeness rule already drops them for most engines, so excluding them uniformly removes an incomparability rather than a result.

ToolRet partitions a query across chunks. Dropping only the over-long chunks would leave the query scored against a reduced candidate set, which is an easier question than the benchmark asks, so the surviving chunks of a partly excluded query are removed with it.

deliberately_not_excluded.CRUXEval: 40 questions whose options differ only by case or whitespace are legitimate: they are Python values, and the case and spacing are exactly what the task tests.
deliberately_not_excluded.MMLU/ARC/GPQA case collisions: genotype notation (BB/Bb/bb), logic predicates (Cs/sC) and variable names (l/L) are semantic; only a case-blind comparison makes them look duplicated.

clarifications: CRUXEval uses the sole frozen output-choice track; the proposal incorrectly mentioned an input track that does not exist in this suite.
Interactive scores use existing frozen pilots and first complete benchmark runs, not the proposed expanded three-repeat protocol.
Reproductions have no interactive runs. Those six benchmarks receive zero only as labeled provisional lower bounds, never an official final ranking.
Unsupported source cases receive zero before chance normalization. F1 uses fixed label universes and conservative missing-label penalties.
All linked requests must succeed for source-case support; no successful-intersection score shortcut.
Point estimates only; paired cluster-bootstrap uncertainty is not yet calculated.
The index panel is the Decision Index 0.2 panel (decision-index-0.2), not the frozen core25 proposal; core25 scores are still computed and kept as frozen_scores.

Benchmarks outside the frozen core25 panel enter with their board score times the answered share (unanswered or unsupported counts as wrong); the 19 core25 static benchmarks keep their case-group coverage adjustment.
steps: Score every benchmark with its own primary metric and adjust it for coverage: an unanswered, refused, errored or unsupported request counts as wrong (for the 19 core25 static benchmarks a case whose linked requests did not all succeed scores zero; for the others the score on answered requests is multiplied by the answered share).
Benchmarks with several tracks (RouterBench 0-shot/5-shot, GSM8K 4-/10-choice) average their tracks equally; iSarcasmEval uses track A English as its headline and track B never enters the index.

Lower-is-better metrics are converted against their baseline: ForecastBench value = clip((0.25 - Brier) / (0.25 - 0)) x coverage, so always predict p = 0.5 (Brier 0.25) or worse scores 0 and a perfect forecast scores 1.

Each of the five areas is the plain mean of its benchmarks: Knowledge & Reasoning (10: GPQA Diamond, GSM8K, ChessBench, MuSR, SATA-Bench, CRUXEval, CLadder, HLE, MMLU-Pro, BBH), Language Understanding (10: ContractNLI, ANLI, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, ACOS, FinEntity, iSarcasmEval, VAST, NLI4CT, RAGTruth), Retrieval & Classification (7: BANKING77, CLINC150, SGD, BRIGHT, Amazon ESCI, PhishNChips, HoVer), Tools & Automation (6: BFCL, ToolRet, API-Bank, RouterBench, Home appliances, When2Call), Arts & Human Taste (7: BPoMP, Humicroedit, POP909, cfcolor, ForecastBench, Habermas, New Yorker).

Chance-correct every benchmark: k = clip((s − chance) / (1 − chance)) with the chance level listed below, so 0 is random guessing and 1 is perfect. Multi-track and retrieval benchmarks correct each track or query against its own chance level; ForecastBench is already 0 at its baseline.

Decision Index = 100 × mean of the five area scores (each the mean of its chance-corrected benchmarks). Every area weighs 0.2 whatever its benchmark count; every benchmark weighs 1 inside its area. 40 benchmarks in all.
Not in the index, still shown on the board: MMLU, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, SimpleBench.

Raw accuracy (not chance-corrected) repeats the same averaging on the uncorrected scores and is shown on model pages; the breadth variant takes a shifted geometric mean of the five chance-corrected area scores and is computed but hidden.
The six interactive environments of the frozen core25 panel stay out for every model, Jev included, because no reproduction has run them.

index.chance_paragraph: The Decision Index is chance-corrected. Every benchmark score is first mapped to (score − chance) / (1 − chance), clipped to 0–1, where chance is what random guessing scores on that benchmark: 0.5 on a yes/no question, 0.25 with four options, the expected nDCG of a random ranking for retrieval, the F1 of random labels for F1-scored tasks. 0 means no better than random guessing and 100 means perfect, so a benchmark made of yes/no questions no longer hands out 50 free points and a benchmark with hundreds of options no longer looks harder than it is. Area scores and the index average these corrected values exactly as before. The raw, uncorrected accuracy is still computed and shown on each model page as raw accuracy (not chance-corrected).
index.panel_change: Decision Index 0.2 replaces the 19-benchmark panel of 0.1 with 40 benchmarks: the static suite minus MMLU, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, SimpleBench, plus the seven benchmarks added in 0.2. Area and benchmark weights stay equal.

evaluation_rules: Native inference helpers, prompts and readout rules are preserved. Mechanical schema translations and any probability conversion are recorded with the adapter.
No prompt tuning, truncation, option pruning, retraining, or correctness-based retry.

Two requests per benchmark/subtrack form the 86-request compatibility pass. It is not a representative accuracy estimate. A model advances only after that pass completes without runtime errors; supported capacity exclusions stay visible.

Entire linked source groups must be complete and supported before they enter the preliminary successful-case scorer. Missing coverage is reported separately. These successful-case metrics must not be directly averaged into an overall index.

Full records retain original state/questions, native outputs, mapped answers, probabilities, errors and CUDA-synchronized request time. Model loading and toy warmup are separate. Compute timing excludes HTTP/network and is not directly equivalent to Jev HTTPS latency.
Decider's eager and compilation-heavy runs are separate. The initial compiled smoke measured compilation at new shapes, not warmed serving latency.
Native abstentions are retained as terminal abstentions; the wrapper never forces them into a listed answer.

Games require fresh episodes using each model's own decisions under the same seeds, observations, options, partners and budgets. **Interactive reproduction runs have not started; do not reuse Jev trajectories as their scores.**

hard_rules.detail: Every request is sent whole. A model whose context window cannot hold a prompt records that request as unsupported; it is never shortened to fit.
The full option set of every question is offered. No option pruning, no candidate reduction, no label-set narrowing per model.
Each entrant runs with its own native inference helpers, prompts and readout rules as published. Mechanical schema translations and any probability conversion are recorded with the adapter.
Gold answers never enter model state; requests.jsonl carries the exact payloads with labels omitted.
Transient transport errors retry up to twice; a valid wrong answer is never retried.
A model that abstains keeps its abstention as a terminal answer; the wrapper never forces it into a listed option.
Unsupported, refused and errored requests score zero against the full denominator. Nobody climbs by skipping the hard cases.

complete_run_gate.rule: A run enters the index only when its status event is "complete" and it has processed at least 120,615 rows (the 121,057-request corpus minus the 442 questions excluded for every engine).

rules.superseded_policy: A model appears once, at the configuration that stands. Lifting a cap the author set outside the model, or replacing a checkpoint, retires the earlier run from the ranking; the results file stays on disk, it just no longer competes.

entrants.principle: Nothing is inferred from a name. The kind comes from what the run recorded it loaded, the base comes from the Hub card's own base_model field or from the run's recorded runtime model, and anything that resolves to neither is left null rather than guessed.

kinds.rule: The entrant published no weights of its own: it serves a stock checkpoint from a base-model vendor namespace (Qwen, Google, LiquidAI, Meta, Mistral, Microsoft, NVIDIA, DeepSeek, AI2, HuggingFaceTB, Answer.AI, OpenAI, IBM Granite, TII) through its own decoding or scoring code.
The entrant's own repo ships whole model weights (.safetensors, .bin, .pt, .pth, .gguf or .npz) with no adapter files.
The entrant's files include adapter_config.json or adapter_model.* and no separate head, scorer or pointer weights.
Adapter files plus a head, scorer or pointer module.
A head, scorer or pointer module on a frozen backbone the entrant did not train; classed as full fine-tune when no base model is recorded.
Own repo with weights the file list could not classify further.

entrants.weights_in_tree: A GitHub entrant that carries trained weights inside its own checkout (for example a scorer adapter) counts as trained, not as a technique over the stock base.

techniques.rule: The executing model class ends in ForCausalLM or ForConditionalGeneration, read from the config of the entrant's own checkpoint or, failing that, of the backbone it rides on.
The model_type or architecture class contains "diffusion", however the model is served.
GLiClass, GLiNER2 (BoundaryExtractor / extractor) and GLiFormer classes, bucketed together for the badge; the exact published class is kept alongside.

parameter_count_precedence: Backbone parameter count from the Hub safetensors metadata of the base model (a LoRA or a head reports the backbone it rides on, which is what it costs to run).
Otherwise the entrant's own repo's safetensors metadata total.
Otherwise an exact count from each safetensors header (shapes read over a range request, no tensor download).
Otherwise, for .bin-only repos, weight bytes divided by the declared torch_dtype width, flagged params_estimated.
Otherwise the size stated in the model name (9B, 350M, 35B-A3B gives the total), flagged params_from_name.
trained_bytes is the entrant's own published weight bytes, which is what separates a 9B full fine-tune from a 9B backbone carrying a few megabytes of adapter.
entrants.base_model_rule: base_model is followed from the Hub card until the owner changes (a card often points at a sibling: an NVFP4 quantization declares the unquantized copy; Decision Lex declares Kai), so the row says what the weights descend from. A base under a vendor namespace that is itself a quantization is resolved two more hops to the original model. The chain is kept for the record.
entrants.naming: Each row uses what the project calls itself in its own README or model card, with the author in parentheses where the name alone is ambiguous (five separate entrants are some spelling of "openjev"). variant names a serving choice made here, never part of the published name.

added_benchmarks.name: BBH
added_benchmarks.framing: The 27 BBH task files minus the four with free-form answers (`dyck_languages`, `multistep_arithmetic_two`, `object_counting`, `word_sorting`) leaves 23 files = 19 task families (the three `logical_deduction_*` and three `tracking_shuffled_objects_*` files are one family each). state = the task input verbatim, including its own `Options:` block; instructions = `CHOICE`. Criteria: the `(A) text` lines parsed from that block (key `(A)`, the published target form), or the `- Yes / - No`, `- valid / - invalid` lines, or for the three tasks that list no options the task's fixed answer set (`boolean_expressions` True/False, `sports_understanding` yes/no, `web_of_lies` Yes/No). No option is invented. Four source items are malformed and excluded before any call, so 5,507 of 5,511 remain: `movie_recommendation:163` (target "Monsters, Inc" was split across options A and B), `ruin_names:99` and `ruin_names:144` (targets containing commas were split into several options, so the gold is not an option), `snarks:88` (input truncated to a single option).
added_benchmarks.licence: MIT (repository LICENSE); carries the BIG-bench canary, never place in training corpora

added_benchmarks.name: RAGTruth
added_benchmarks.chance_note: F1 of a fair coin; accuracy chance 0.5; always-hallucinated F1 0.518; majority-class accuracy 0.651
added_benchmarks.framing: All 2,700 test responses (900 each of QA, Summary, Data2txt; six responder models). state = `{prompt, response}`, where `prompt` is the exact generation prompt from `source_info.jsonl` (it carries the passages, article or structured data) and `response` is the evaluated response. Question is a `noul`: instructions `The response contains content that is not supported by the context in the prompt.`; criteria true `The response contains content that is not supported by the context in the prompt.`, false `All content of the response is supported by the context in the prompt.` Gold = hallucinated iff the response has at least one annotated span (`len(labels) > 0`, exactly the RAGTruth baseline's `is_halu`); 943 positives. Spans flagged `implicit_true` or `due_to_null` count, as in the baseline. Responses marked `incorrect_refusal`/`truncated` are kept. Headline metric: F1 on the hallucinated class (prediction = P(yes) ≥ 0.5), plus accuracy.
added_benchmarks.licence: MIT annotations and code; contexts include CNN/Daily Mail, MS MARCO (non-commercial) and the Yelp Open Dataset (redistribution forbidden): built locally, rows not republished

added_benchmarks.name: HoVer
added_benchmarks.framing: All 4,000 dev claims (2,000 SUPPORTED, 2,000 NOT_SUPPORTED). The dataset provides evidence as `supporting_facts` = (Wikipedia title, sentence id) pairs into the HoVer authors' own Wikipedia introduction database (`wiki_wo_links.db`, distributed by the HoVer authors and pinned by sha256). Sentence ids refer to a CoreNLP split that is not distributed, so rather than re-splitting, state carries the **complete introduction of every document named in `supporting_facts`**: `{claim, evidence: [{title, text}]}`, documents in first-mention order. Only dataset-provided text is used; no retrieval, no external text, and NOT_SUPPORTED claims get their own annotated documents just like SUPPORTED ones. This is the oracle-document setting, easier than HoVer's open retrieval setting. instructions `Is the claim supported by the evidence?`; criteria `SUPPORTED` → `The evidence supports the claim.`, `NOT_SUPPORTED` → `The evidence does not support the claim.` (the original label strings as keys).
added_benchmarks.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 data, MIT code, Wikipedia text CC BY-SA: share-alike applies to republished rows

added_benchmarks.name: When2Call
added_benchmarks.framing: All 3,652 `mcq` test items. state = `{tools, question}` with `tools` = the item's `tools` field parsed from JSON strings (not `orig_tools`; 258 items have no tools). instructions `Which response should the assistant give to the user's question, given the available tools?`; criteria `A`..`D` = the four published answers in published order (direct, tool_call, request_for_info, cannot_answer). Category names are not on the wire. Gold is never `A` (direct) by the dataset's construction. Reported: accuracy, macro-F1 over the three gold categories, and tool-call rate when no tools are supplied.

added_benchmarks.framing: `matching` config (fold 0) test, 528 items. Text only, no pixels: state = `{scene, description, uncanny_description, entities}` = the dataset's `image_location`, `image_description`, `image_uncanny_description`, `entities` (Wikipedia URLs as published). instructions `Which caption was written for this cartoon?`; criteria `A`..`E` = `caption_choices` in order.
